Shanghai/Ningbo.waitLabel: SNH 4-7 days · NGB 3-5 days (as of 12 Aug)
Shanghai/Ningbo.note: Waigaoqiao, Yangshan and Ningbo-Zhoushan have been fully open since 10-11 August, so this is backlog rather than closure. The 3-7 day range is SEKO's from 12 August and is now thirteen days old — indicative only, nobody has published a newer figure. Two things changed this run. Bunkering at Zhoushan's outer anchorages, Tiaozhoumen and Xiazhimen, has been suspended since the weekend on rough weather from three successive cyclones, with no resumption timeline; the inner anchorages are still working. And Saudel's forecast track now brings it within roughly 414 km of the port in three days, against 470 km a run ago. A 940 hPa, 85 kt typhoon arriving on top of a queue that has not cleared is the main risk in this dataset.
Shanghai/Ningbo.source: SEKO Asia-Pacific Logistics Monitoring Center, 12 Aug 2026 10:30 HKT; ENGINE, 24 Aug 2026; JMA TC2621 forecast track, 25 Aug 06:40 JST

Xiamen.event: Tropical Depression Gaenari (Typhoon Saudel behind it)
Xiamen.note: Gaenari has moved inland over South China and weakened to a tropical depression at 1000 hPa; the JMA analysis position sits about 120 km from the port and is tracking west-southwest, away from it. No terminal suspension has been announced and no source publishes a Xiamen berth-wait figure. The real question is Saudel, forecast to pass within about 199 km in roughly four days — the closest approach of any system to any tracked port in the current feed.
Xiamen.source: JMA TC2623 and TC2621 specifications, 25 Aug 2026 04:10 and 06:40 JST

Haiphong.note: Narra stalled over the Gulf of Tonkin and is now tracking north-northeast away from the port — 171 km at analysis, widening to 279 km in a day and 384 km in two — and is weakening as it moves inland over Guangxi. Northern Vietnam rainfall was easing by 24 August. Quang Ninh suspended sea-going vessel permits on 22 August and Haiphong put 11,000 response personnel in the field, but no closure of Haiphong's container terminals was announced and no source gives a berth-wait figure. Status is recovering rather than suspended because the disruption was a precautionary stop to sea traffic, not a terminal shutdown.
Haiphong.source: JMA TC2622 specifications, 25 Aug 2026 07:10 JST; DTiNews and VietnamPlus, 22-24 Aug 2026

Shenzhen (Yantian).event: Tropical Storm Narra, Typhoon Saudel, Tropical Depression Gaenari
Shenzhen (Yantian).note: Three systems now sit inside the 600 km ring — Gaenari at 352 km on the current analysis, Narra at 407 km in about two days, Saudel at 359 km in about four — but none of the forecast tracks puts a core over the port and operations are normal. Watch is precautionary. The 2-4 day wait is still SEKO's 12 August figure and has not been refreshed since.
Shenzhen (Yantian).source: SEKO Asia-Pacific Logistics Monitoring Center, 12 Aug 2026 10:30 HKT; JMA TC2621, TC2622 and TC2623 forecast tracks, 25 Aug 2026

remarks: Four systems are active in the JMA feed and three of them sit near the China coast. No tracked port changed status this run except Haiphong, which moves from watch to recovering now that Narra has passed and is weakening inland over Guangxi. Shanghai/Ningbo is still recovering; Xiamen and Shenzhen are still on watch.

Saudel is the one that matters. At 940 hPa and 85 kt sustained with 120 kt gusts it is the only true typhoon in the group, and its track keeps creeping west — 414 km from Shanghai/Ningbo in three days against 470 km a run ago, and 199 km from Xiamen. Taiwan has already suspended 55 ferry services on four routes ahead of it.

The berth-wait figures on this page are stale and should be read that way. SEKO has not updated its monitoring page since 12 August, thirteen days ago, and Kuehne+Nagel's latest weekly gives a number for Busan (1.38 days, BNCT laden yard above 100%) but none for Shanghai, Ningbo, Xiamen, Qingdao or Yantian. Nothing newer exists, so nothing newer is shown.

Zhoushan's outer bunkering anchorages have been shut since the weekend with no restart date. That does not stop container work, but it complicates vessel turnarounds at a port still digesting the Dolphin backlog.
Congestion data resumed after a week-long gap — Linerlytica published 17-23 August in one go, so this run added seven days at once.
